code.text: Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked

note.text: Synthetic teaching-case problem. Evidence grade S. Historical claims: CLM-0009.

code.text: Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration

code.text: He wants to know quickly and plainly whether the spot on the scan is cancer, and what can be done
He has smoked for 35 years, has failed to stop twice on his own, and worries that stopping now is pointless
No doctor had offered him a lung scan before; he wants the same care anyone else would get, without delay
He wants to keep speaking to young people and to keep walking every morning
No known allergy

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Varenicline 0.5 mg oral tablet: one tablet daily for three days, then one tablet twice daily for four days (starting week), with a quit date on day 8

dosageInstruction.text: 0.5 mg daily on days 1 to 3, then 0.5 mg twice daily on days 4 to 7

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Varenicline 1 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth twice daily after food, for 12 weeks and then a further 12 weeks to prevent relapse
Nivolumab 360 mg intravenous infusion over 30 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for three cycles before surgery (one 240 mg and one 120 mg vial)

dosageInstruction.text: Day 1 every 21 days for three cycles

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Carboplatin 10 mg/mL injection, 525 mg (AUC 5 by the Calvert formula, creatinine clearance 80 mL/min) intravenously on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for three cycles

dosageInstruction.text: Day 1 every 21 days for three cycles

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 (970 mg for a body surface area of 1.94 m2) intravenously over 10 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, for three cycles

dosageInstruction.text: Day 1 every 21 days for three cycles

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Folic acid 1 mg oral tablet, one tablet daily from one week before the first pemetrexed dose until three weeks after the last
Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) 1000 mcg intramuscular injection, one dose a week before the first pemetrexed dose (repeat every nine weeks while on pemetrexed)

dosageInstruction.text: 1000 mcg once; a second dose was not due before pemetrexed ended

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Dexamethasone 4 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice daily on the day before, the day of and the day after each pemetrexed dose

dosageInstruction.text: 4 mg twice daily for three days around each cycle

medicationCodeableConcept.text: Ondansetron 8 mg oral tablet, one tablet every 8 hours as needed for nausea during chemotherapy
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets every 8 hours as needed for pain after surgery

code.text: Shared decision-making visit for lung cancer screening with a decision aid (benefits, false positives, overdiagnosis, radiation, and the need for yearly scans and for tobacco treatment); he chose to be screened

coding.display: Low dose computed tomography of chest without contrast

code.text: Low-dose CT of the chest without contrast for lung cancer screening (first screen): solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe; enlarged left hilar lymph node 1.6 cm in short axis; mild centrilobular emphysema in both upper lobes; coronary artery calcification, moderate; Lung-RADS 4X (category 4B with additional features of malignancy)
Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: the left upper lobe nodule is smaller than on the screening CT; no new opacity, consolidation or ground-glass change; no effusion
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with his consent

coding.display: Positron emission tomography with computed tomography using fluorodeoxyglucose (18-F)

code.text: FDG PET-CT: avid left upper lobe nodule, 2.9 cm (SUVmax 9.8); avid left interlobar (11L) node, 1.6 cm (SUVmax 6.1); no avid mediastinal, supraclavicular or contralateral node; no distant uptake. The infrarenal abdominal aorta measures 2.1 cm
MRI of the brain with contrast: no metastases

coding.display: Endoscopic endobronchial ultrasonography guided transbronchial needle aspiration of mediastinal lymph node

code.text: Endobronchial ultrasound with systematic needle aspiration of stations 4R, 4L, 7, 10L and 11L under moderate sedation: adenocarcinoma in 11L (TTF-1 positive); 4R, 4L, 7 and 10L negative with adequate lymphocytes; PD-L1 (22C3) tumor proportion score 40 percent; tissue next-generation sequencing (reported in six days, with concordant plasma testing): KRAS G12C mutation, STK11 and KEAP1 wild type; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration

Thoracic multidisciplinary tumor board (thoracic surgery, medical and radiation oncology, pulmonology, radiology, pathology, nurse navigator): resectable cT1c N1 M0 stage IIB adenocarcinoma, no EGFR or ALK alteration; recommends three cycles of nivolumab with platinum doublet chemotherapy, restaging, then lobectomy

Pulmonary function tests: spirometry and DLCO (FEV1 2.71 L, 86 percent predicted; FEV1/FVC 0.73; DLCO 86 percent predicted). Predicted postoperative values after left upper lobectomy (14 of 19 segments remaining): FEV1 63 percent and DLCO 63 percent
Pulmonary rehabilitation as prehabilitation during chemoimmunotherapy: 16 supervised sessions of aerobic and strength training with breathing exercises, twice weekly

coding.display: CT of chest and upper abdomen with contrast

code.text: Restaging CT of the chest and upper abdomen with contrast after three cycles: left upper lobe nodule 1.3 cm (from 2.9 cm); left interlobar node 0.8 cm (from 1.6 cm); no new nodule, node, effusion or ground-glass change; no liver or adrenal lesion

coding.display: Lobectomy of upper lobe of left lung

code.text: Video-assisted thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal (stations 4L, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) and hilar lymph node dissection; three days in hospital without complications. Pathology: ypT1a N0 (0 of 16 nodes; treatment effect without viable tumor in the 11L node), 0.7 cm residual adenocarcinoma with 6 percent viable tumor (major pathologic response), margins clear (R0)
Pulmonary rehabilitation after lobectomy: a 12-week program, twice weekly, started

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Referral to thoracic oncology: consultation within two weeks to review the screening CT, PET-CT and EBUS results with him and plan treatment
  • Work-up of the Lung-RADS 4X nodule without delay: FDG PET-CT and brain MRI with contrast this week, then endobronchial ultrasound with systematic sampling of mediastinal and hilar nodes (at least stations 4R, 4L and 7, and any PET-avid node), with enough tissue for PD-L1 and comprehensive next-generation sequencing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK, HER2) and plasma testing in parallel; nurse navigator to track each date
  • Tobacco treatment at every visit: brief advice, varenicline offered with a quit date, the Arizona quitline and counseling; stopping smoking improves outcomes even after a lung cancer diagnosis
  • Equity safeguards: a nurse navigator, written results and next steps at each visit, transport and cost help offered, and time from scan to treatment tracked against the goal
  • Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain information he can share, and advance care planning when he is ready
  • Chemoimmunotherapy before surgery: nivolumab 360 mg with carboplatin (AUC 5) and pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 every three weeks for three cycles, with folic acid, vitamin B12 and dexamethasone premedication, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests first, and restaging CT before surgery
  • Immune-related adverse event monitoring: TSH, free T4, liver tests, creatinine, glucose and blood count before each cycle, morning cortisol at baseline and before surgery, and a written list of warning symptoms with a 24-hour oncology line
  • Physiologic evaluation for lobectomy (spirometry and DLCO with predicted postoperative values) and prehabilitation: a pulmonary rehabilitation program during chemotherapy
  • Thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal and hilar lymph node dissection after restaging shows response and no new disease
  • After surgery: no further systemic therapy after a major pathologic response, by shared decision; history, examination and chest CT every six months for two to three years, then yearly low-dose CT; pulmonary rehabilitation after surgery; the KRAS G12C result kept on file for any recurrence

resource.title: Jesse Owens synthetic care plan
resource.description: Find lung cancer early in a 65-year-old Black man who has smoked a pack a day for 35 years and who was never offered screening: confirm eligibility on the USPSTF 1974 criteria (50 to 80 years, 20 pack-years or more, smoking now or quit within 15 years), hold the shared decision-making visit with a decision aid and tobacco treatment that the CMS coverage decision requires, read the low-dose CT with Lung-RADS, and work up a category 4X nodule without delay: PET-CT, brain MRI, systematic EBUS staging of the mediastinum (ACCP), and tissue for PD-L1 and comprehensive biomarker testing before any immunotherapy. Then treat resectable stage IIB adenocarcinoma on the NCCN guideline: tumor board review, physiologic evaluation for lobectomy (ACCP), three cycles of nivolumab with carboplatin and pemetrexed before surgery (CheckMate 816), immune-related adverse event monitoring, thoracoscopic lobectomy with lymph node dissection, and surveillance CT; treat tobacco dependence with varenicline even after the diagnosis; and track each step for delay, because Black Americans are less often found eligible for and offered screening and less often offered surgery for early lung cancer.
